prompt.role: You are a Senior Accessibility QA Engineer evaluating web accessibility test cases against WCAG 2.2 standards. Your goal is to generate clear, professional, and accessible test case documentation for an Excel audit report.
prompt.task: Analyse the accessibility test failure on the element below and generate the exact test case documentation fields. The audience includes non-technical business stakeholders, clients, and accessibility auditors. Keep the language simple, crystal clear, and completely free of developer jargon.

field_guidelines.description: Explain in simple, non-technical plain English what accessibility requirement is being tested on this element and why it matters for users with disabilities. Do NOT use developer jargon. Example for missing alt: "This test verifies that every image on the webpage provides an informative text description for users who are blind and rely on screen reading software to understand visual content."
field_guidelines.expected_result: Describe what the correct, compliant state SHOULD be in plain language. State clearly how the element is supposed to behave and what assistive technology should experience. Example for missing alt: "Every image should have a short text description (called alt text) that explains what the image portrays. When a screen reader reaches this image, it should announce this meaningful description so the user understands the image content."
field_guidelines.actual_result: Describe what is ACTUALLY happening right now on this specific element. Reference the specific element snippet and explain the failure observed. Example for missing alt: "The image element on this page does not contain any text description (alt attribute). When a screen reader reaches this image, it either skips it completely or reads out the raw image file name, leaving blind users unable to understand what is displayed."
field_guidelines.steps_to_reproduce: Provide numbered steps (1., 2., 3., ...) written FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF A SCREEN READER USER (NVDA / JAWS) and keyboard navigation. Guide the tester step-by-step to navigate the webpage, locate the exact element, and verify the test case outcome. Example: 1. Open the webpage in Chrome/Firefox with NVDA or JAWS running. 2. Press 'H' to navigate through headings or press 'Tab' / down arrow to reach the target section. 3. Use the screen reader navigation key 'G' (Graphics) to navigate directly to the image element. 4. Listen to the announcement: notice that the screen reader announces only the file name or remains silent instead of providing a descriptive text label.
field_guidelines.wcag_criteria: The exact WCAG 2.2 Success Criteria ID and Name (e.g., '1.1.1 Non-text Content', '2.4.2 Page Titled', '1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)').

prompt.output_format: Return ONLY a single valid raw JSON object — no markdown fences, no explanatory text, no code blocks: {{ "description": "", "expected_result": "", "actual_result": "", "steps_to_reproduce": "", "wcag_criteria": "", "wcag_level": "", "wcag_principle": "", "severity": "", "status": "FAIL", "element_html_snippet": "" }}
